title: Clinical Genomic Scientist I - R&D Innovation
description:
SHIFT:

Day (United States of America)

Seeking Breakthrough Makers

Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) offers countless ways to change lives. Our diverse community of more than 20,000 Breakthrough Makers will inspire you to pursue passions, develop expertise, and drive innovation.

At CHOP, your experience is valued; your voice is heard; and your contributions make a difference for patients and families. Join us as we build on our promise to advance pediatric care—and your career.


CHOP does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, religion, or any other legally protected categories in any employment, training, or vendor decisions or programs. CHOP recognizes the critical importance of a workforce rich in varied backgrounds and experiences and engages in ongoing efforts to achieve that through equally varied and non-discriminatory means.


A Brief Overview

The Genomic Diagnostic Laboratory (GDL) of the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia is seeking a highly motivated Clinical Genomic Scientist (CGS) with an interest in clinical genomics and laboratory diagnostics to join our team. This is an exciting opportunity to work collaboratively within the Research and Development (R&D) Innovation team and together with our laboratory directors, supervisors, analysts, genetic counselors and wet bench team to develop, validate, and launch cutting edge technologies and which have a direct impact on establishing the diagnosis, prognosis, treatment, and management plan for our patients. This position will also include performing clinical test development and clinical research. The ability to communicate in a highly matrixed environment will be key to the candidate’s success. Seasoned professionals are welcome to apply and will be considered for the career ladder position commensurate with their experience. This position requires several days per week onsite at our Philadelphia campus.

The Clinical Genomic Scientist I is primarily focused on developing and validating wet bench protocols and data analysis workflows to support clinical test development within genomics. The scope of the work will include the development, improvement, QC, troubleshooting and optimization of wet bench workflows and processes, establishing data analysis workflows and troubleshooting, as well as presentation of results for multi-omics-based tests. The position allows for a wide variety of activities described within the job responsibilities. Activities occur with a moderate degree of supervision with moderate latitude for independent judgment.

The Clinical Genomic Scientist I position is an entry level position for a Genomic Scientist. The focus of the position is analysis of complex genomic data in diagnostic settings. The position allows for a wide variety of activities described within the job responsibilities. All activities occur with a moderate degree of supervision with some latitude for independent judgment, development of genetic testing workflows and processes, and presentation of results.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • Experience with Next Generation Sequencing (Illumina)
  • Experience with Long Read Sequencing (PacBio)
  • Experience with molecular biology techniques such as DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, cell culture, qPCR, ddPCR, NGS library preparation, and related QC/troubleshooting
  • Experience in assay development and validation
  • Background in genomics or related field
  • Strong presentation skills

What you will do

  • Primary Responsibilities:
  • Accurately performs clinical correlation of gene/variant with patient phenotype, variant classification, scientific literature review, and/or report writing for genomic tests of the high complexity, including but not limited to chromosomal SNP array, exome/genome analysis, and NGS/exome-based panels.
  • Supports refinement or update of existing analysis workflows/protocols in order to improve sensitivity, efficiency and quality of testing.
  • Supports new test development efforts of the laboratory. Designs and conducts validation experiments, analyzes validation data and write high quality validation reports. Defines quantitative metrics and thresholds for quality control and establish quality assurance program for the newly developed tests.
  • Performs quality control testing and maintain quality management programs according to written protocols and policies. Reviews results for accuracy prior to acceptance. Recognizes and resolves abnormal, unusual or unexpected results; appropriately identify issues that require further action by the Supervisor, Manager or Director. Completes, evaluates and records all appropriate quality controls and quality assurance markers. Activates troubleshooting procedures when necessary.
  • Assists others (as appropriate based on skill level) by demonstrating expertise of advance experience and or training as necessary for laboratory operation. Evaluates new protocols, methods, techniques and/or equipment and makes recommendations to the Director, Manager or Supervisor. Prepares technical documentation drafts for publication and/or procedure manuals.
  • Additional responsibilities:
  • Prepares and presents technical education and case presentations to laboratory or medical staff. Participates in education/mentorship of other laboratory staff through direct interaction and presentations. May publish/present scientific presentations/papers at a national level. Prepares and presents data at Rounds, meetings, Con Eds.
  • Provides professional, courteous and calm customer service to both internal and external customers. Identifies appropriate resources and sources for re-directed inquiries. Responds appropriately and professionally to technical inquiries and requests for information: refers caller to Supervisor/Director/Manager when required. Acts as a reference source for laboratory procedures within their skill inventory as necessary. Takes charge of any unusual or problem situations and reports issue to Supervisor, Manager or Director. Follows privacy rules (HIPAA) as defined by the hospital policy. Interacts with co-workers, hospital staff and all others (via various communication methods) in ways that foster professionalism, efficiency and optimal patient care.
  • Regularly reviews operational procedure manuals, individual competency assessment, quality assurance monitors for completeness, accuracy and regulatory compliance. Assists the Supervisor/Manager with recommendations for content, accuracy and improvements and makes changes as directed. Actively participates in laboratory section continuing education/quality assurance meetings by preparing and presenting presentations related to their work. Assist the Supervisor/Manager with the preparation of competency assessment tools.
  • May also be involved in research activities, including abstract/manuscript submission and presentations at local or national professional conferences, related to a specialized patient population, disease area, genetic pathway or testing technology.

Education Qualifications

  • Master's Degree Genetics, Molecular Biology or related field - Required
  • Doctorate Genetics, Molecular Biology or related field - Preferred

Experience Qualifications

  • At least three (3) years relevant experience - Required
  • At least three (3) years relevant experience - Required
  • Clinical laboratory or research experience in a disease area, genetic pathway or genomic testing technology - Preferred

Skills and Abilities

  • Advanced analytic skills, preferably demonstrated by peer-reviewed publications
  • High level accountability and attention to details
  • Excellent organization and communication skills
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment
  • Knowledge of the working mechanism of microarray, NGS, mass spectrometry, or other high-throughput technologies
  • Familiarity with resources of genomic data sets and analysis tools, such as UCSC Genome Browser, HGMD, ClinVar, Alamut and NCBI databases

title: Full-spectrum Doula (Vallejo, CA)
description:
Loula is seeking experienced full-spectrum doulas to join our growing network of independent doula providers! You must complete this interest form to move forward in our process! We're excited to hear from you!

✨ About Loula

With a network of over 500 experienced and diverse doulas, Loula is building the leading provider network for birth and postpartum doula care. We partner with both Medicaid and commercial health insurance plans to make it easier for doulas to accept health insurance without the administrative burden.

Loula offers full-service support for Medicaid enrollment, credentialing, insurance verification, medical billing, and payment to doulas in California. By taking on the operational complexity, Loula empowers doulas to focus on what matters most: delivering exceptional care.

We believe every birthing person deserves access to high-quality doula support, not just those who can afford to pay out of pocket. Our mission is to help doulas build thriving practices while making it possible for insured families to access the care they deserve.

💰 Why Partner with Loula?

We partner with our doulas every step of the way:

  • How much can I make? Up to $134/hour of billable time, with rates varying by payer and plan.

  • Direct deposits twice a month. Don't worry about denied claims! We pay you regardless of claim outcomes, so you're never left waiting on payers to get paid.

  • Free, hassle-free credentialing: We get you credentialed with major Medicaid and commercial insurance plans in California, at no cost to you.

  • Client referrals, not cold outreach: Get referrals to insured clients through our client referral/doula matching program. Let our Care Navigator introduce you to amazing clients, no marketing spend required on your end.

  • Build your own practice, your way: You're an independent contractor in a non-exclusive network, so keep your own clients and practice alongside your work with Loula.

  • No minimums, no pressure: There are no client minimums or visit requirements. You decide how much or how little to take on.

  • Admin? Handled: We manage insurance verification, billing, and payment so you can spend your time with clients, not paperwork.

  • You're not alone: Join a network of experienced doulas with access to shared resources, community, and ongoing support.

🛠 Minimum Qualifications

You'll need one of the following:

  • Completed 16 hours of birth doula training AND attended 3 births as a doula, OR

  • 5 years of experience as a doula, with 3 letters of recommendation

You'll also need:

  • Adult and infant CPR training

  • HIPAA training

  • Liability insurance

If you don't yet have CPR training, HIPAA training, liability insurance, or the letters of recommendation, you can still reach out! We can support you in getting set up with these requirements.

Please note that if you are not located in California and/or do not meet the minimum qualifications listed above, we will be unable to move forward with an introductory meeting.

📝 Application Process

How can I learn more about partnering with Loula?

  1. Click this link to submit an interest form and start the process

  2. You'll be prompted to complete a few basic screening questions

  3. If you meet the minimum qualifications, you'll be invited to schedule a call with our team

  4. During this conversation, we'll get to know you, your experience, and your practice goals, and share more about how Loula works. This is meant to assess whether a partnership is a strong mutual fit.

Loula is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.

title: Principal Key Account Representative - Amazon Account
description:
ABOUT THE POSITION

The SOREL Sales team partners with external partners (from wholesale key accounts to independent boutiques) and internal teams including Merchandising, Marketing, and Design to understand the needs of consumers and the realities of the marketplace, as well as how our product best fits in to that equation. The Sales team’s business savviness and sales strategy expertise lends itself to strong partnerships and solid results.

As member of the Sales team the Principal Key Account Representative drives sales strategies to support our Amazon account. Uses an enterprise mindset to optimize profitability for both the company and Amazon account. Responsibilities include account presentations, collaborating to analyze/plan account’s financials and in-season management. Additional responsibilities include assortment planning, assisting with projecting and tracking inventory needs and on hands for future production.

HOW YOU’LL MAKE A DIFFERENCE

  • Manage all aspects of the Amazon account by developing and implementing sales strategies that promote the sale and sell through of SOREL product.

  • Drives sustainable and profitable sales growth for Amazon's strategic account.

  • Harvests and cultivates sales opportunities by leveraging analytics and aligning brand priorities.

  • Use sales analytics, product, consumer, and marketplace expertise to construct compelling seasonal Go-to-Market plans. Provides associated business forecasts to internal stakeholders.

  • Partners and collaborates with internal and external cross-functional teams to run a best-in-class business.

  • Develops growth strategies that align to brand expectations and deliver on goals of increased market share, while elevating brand equity. Partners with leadership to develop short-term growth strategies and provides input into long-term strategies.

  • Uses elevated and persuasive storytelling and directive selling techniques to deliver compelling seasonal product presentations.

  • Executes and collaborates with internal and external partners to create and implement marketing plans that build consumer awareness, drive conversion, and lead to brand advocacy.

  • Leverages marketplace intelligence and consumer insights to create, execute, and shares best practices for activating brand strategy.

  • Financial Planning – Understands all components of an upfront financial plan for an account/department and be able to develop a plan for each account. Receipt flow and understanding of retail math are key components

  • Performs financial analysis of in-season key metrics, analyzing and managing sell through in season and makes recommendations on order shifts and flows to positively affect the seasonal financials

  • Works closely with key accounts to establish appropriate sales goals based on sales history analysis and projected sales trends

  • Meets regularly with the buying and management teams of key accounts to project and manage inventory on hand and purchase needs. Meets regularly with SOREL sales management to review sales data and account management.

  • Uses strong presentation skills to tell the brand story, initiative stories and product specific presentation at the selling table

  • Works closely with SOREL departments to coordinate product presentations and provide information on technical aspects of product including design and materials.

  • Manages sales order entry, bulk management, auto replenishment forecasts and order flow and fulfillment

  • Works closely with an internal SOREL team of merchants, customer service and planning that is responsible for product planning and production, sales and inventory projections, SMU design, operational and logistics support, and information to all parties to help properly manage key account business.

  • Understands and facilitates implementation of key on-line marketing strategies

  • Manage all on-line sales components including Brand landing pages, site SKU management and product descriptions

  • Responsible for strategies to maintain profitability including off price and promotional offers

  • Understand the competition and able to communicate the issues that arise from our competitors to management/merchandising

YOU ARE

  • Familiar with standard concepts, practices, and procedures within the sales field.

  • Strong in written and verbal communication

  • Able to handle and work with proprietary, private, and confidential information.

  • An out of the box thinker and willing to challenge the status quo – creative ideas and solutions preferred

YOU HAVE

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or equivalent combination of education and experience

  • 8+ years’ experience in sales of footwear and/or apparel industry experience.

  • 5+ years Amazon Fashion account experience required.

  • Thorough knowledge of marketing, sales theory, strategy, prospecting, account business planning, forecasting, use of sales aids, and closing techniques

  • Knowledge of product lines/services and outdoor industry

  • Proven experience in defining retailer value add from markets, outdoor industry, product trends and key data

  • Experience leading business reviews and creating marketing plans

  • Advanced interpersonal skills, including the ability to quickly build relationships.

  • The ability to travel 25% of the time.

description:

From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Coordinated Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!

As a Coordinated Property Adjuster, you will be dedicated to providing exceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will be handling escalated claims files involving complex contents damage to ensure our customers receive the highest level of support and resolution for these claims.

  • Handle escalated claims files involving complex contents damage.

  • Conduct a thorough coverage investigation of the loss and ensure the policy was applied correctly.

  • Use advanced video technology to collaborate with onsite vendors to identify damages and write a contents damage estimate.

  • Communicate empathetically with customers and help them through their claim process in a fast, fair, and easy manner.

  • Negotiate claim settlements with customers in accordance with business unit standard methodologies.

  • Coordinate with structure and ALE adjusters to ensure holistic handling of the claim file.

  • Use data and analytics to tell a story and influence decision making.

  • If offered the role, you will go through virtual training. You will receive ongoing support, mentoring and coaching as you develop your career.

You'll wear a few hats that will require a level of experience:

  • The Customer Service Expert –you’ll live into Allstate’s Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each Property claim. You lead with empathy, always.

  • The Investigator – you’ll confidently and independently investigate property claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.

  • The Effective Communicator – you’ll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. You’ll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.

  • The Negotiator – You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.

  • The Problem Solver –you’ll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.

  • The Recorder – you’ll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained in. You’ll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Schedule:

  • Monday – Friday; 8 am - 5 pm with rotational weekend duty, Saturday or Sunday.

  • This role involves taking care of customers in their times of need. As a result, you must be willing to work some weekend and extended hours if necessary.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Reside in Columbus, OH area.

  • 3+ years of previous experience handling property insurance claims preferred.

  • Have prior experience using estimating software like Xactimate for complex contents estimating.

  • Value providing an effortless customer service experience.

  • You enjoy the ability to work independently in the field or from your home office.

  • View problems and setbacks as opportunities for improvement and look forward to coming up with creative solutions.

  • Are organized and able to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.

  • Are known for clear and professional communication – both written and verbal.

Required Qualifications:

  • Required to have a valid driver's license and willingness to travel as part of the job requirements.

  • Residency within the posted location is mandatory for this role.

You’re provided with comprehensive training:

  • The training program is designed to help you build a claims foundation and understand the systems and processes in your day-to-day work.

  • Ongoing training opportunities for continuous improvement happen regularly on the job.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor. If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.

  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

  • As a requirement of employment, individuals who currently hold an active insurance license must terminate all existing appointments prior to onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments at any point during employment.

  • Applicants seeking an adjuster role who also hold a resident producer license must formally surrender that license when instructed to by the licensing team. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and accept these licensing requirements and agree to comply.

Sign On Bonus:

You may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.

**Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Based on our Company Car Guidelines, this role may qualify for a company car. Our leadership team determines this based on annual work mileage for this location. You may be required to use your personal vehicle until these guidelines are met. We offer mileage reimbursements for personal vehicle usage during work.

Allstate Benefits:

  • Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as an Allstater, you’ll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:

  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.

  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.

  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role.

  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit: www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

title: Tax & Compliance Specialist
description:
Traild: Who are we?

Traild is a high-growth SaaS company redefining how finance teams operate, combining AI, automation, and payments infrastructure to power the future of B2B finance.

Every year, businesses lose billions to fraud, errors, and mistakes. Traild exists to solve this at scale, helping finance teams move faster, stay in control, and operate with confidence.

With rapid customer growth, global expansion across APAC, North America and EMEA, and continued investment in product innovation, we are at a defining stage of our journey.

This is an opportunity to help shape the next category leader in finance automation, control and security, building technology that transforms how businesses manage, move, and protect money. At the core of this is a powerful AI-driven platform, enabling finance teams to deploy intelligent agents that do the work, surface risk in real time, and continuously improve how financial operations run.

Traild is building the infrastructure behind modern finance, protecting and powering meaningful volumes of the world’s B2B transactions.

If you’re excited by high growth, real ownership, and building something that matters, Traild is the place to do the most impactful work of your career.

Hear how Traild customers speak about us here.


The Role: Want to be a part of our exciting growth journey?

We are looking for a talented, passionate, and motivated individual to join our team as a Tax & Compliance Specialist, where you will play a critical role in keeping Traild's tax and statutory obligations on time and audit-ready as the group scales across regions, in the Finance team.

You will own the group's multi-jurisdiction compliance calendar across Australia, the US, Canada and Israel, coordinate our external tax advisors from preparation through to lodgement, and prepare the company secretarial and insurance work that Legal reviews and signs off.

The ideal candidate will have a strong technical tax background they can apply in unfamiliar jurisdictions, the organisation to run a high-volume lodgement calendar without a deadline slipping, and the confidence to question external advisors rather than take their work at face value.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the tax compliance tracker in Asana as the single source of truth for every obligation across the group, keeping due dates, statuses and owners current.
  • Prepare and lodge Australian obligations, including quarterly BAS, the annual income tax return, the R&D Tax Incentive claim, FBT, Employee Share Scheme reporting and TPAR, with support from our external tax advisors.
  • Coordinate US federal, state and payroll tax filings with advisors and our payroll provider, and maintain sales tax registrations and nexus positions.
  • Coordinate corporate income tax, payroll and indirect tax filings for group entities outside Australia and the US, including Canada and Israel.
  • Assess registration and permanent establishment exposure when Traild hires, contracts or sells into a new jurisdiction, and escalate technical positions early.
  • Coordinate the annual transfer pricing memo refresh and keep intercompany agreements current as the group structure changes.
  • Prepare ASIC lodgements, corporate register updates and board resolution templates for Legal to review and file.
  • Coordinate the annual insurance renewal cycle with our broker, compiling the financial, headcount and risk information each policy needs, for Legal's sign-off.
  • Maintain the compliance evidence archive in SharePoint so signed returns, workpapers and lodgement confirmations are retrievable for audit.
  • Write and maintain SOPs for every recurring filing, so the process holds up as new entities and obligations are added.
  • Monitor tax legislation changes across the jurisdictions Traild operates in and flag what they mean for the group.

Who You Are:

  • Four or more years in corporate tax and compliance, ideally built in a Big 4 or mid-tier practice, including work on Australian client obligations.
  • A degree in accounting, tax or finance. CA, CPA or equivalent qualification preferred.
  • Strong enough on tax fundamentals to apply legislation you have not worked with before. We do not expect experience in every jurisdiction we operate in.
  • Deadline-driven and organised. You know what is due this month across every entity, and nobody needs to ask you for a status update.
  • Comfortable managing external advisors: chasing them, questioning advice that does not stack up, and building in enough time for proper review before lodgement.
  • Experience with Xero, Asana and SharePoint, or close equivalents. Exposure to Anrok or another US sales tax platform is a bonus.
  • Happy working independently in a small finance team, and comfortable raising a better way of doing something rather than working around the problem.
  • Clear written and spoken English, with the judgement to know what to handle alone and what to escalate.
  • Strong collaborator with an attitude embracing growth, hands-on execution, adaptability, and the scale-up spirit.

The Perks of Working at Traild

  • Flexibility: we offer a range of remote, hybrid and flexible working options.

  • Global team: we are growing across APAC, NA and EMEA and have team all across the world.

  • We are growing at an exponential rate, this is an opportunity to get involved with a true rocketship with all the excitement and opportunities that comes with it

  • Our team genuinely loves working at Traild: our eNPS score is 78, where anything above 50 is considered world-class.

Please note that the final applicants for this job will be asked to consent in writing to a police check / criminal background check to the extent permitted by law in your jurisdiction of employment. Please note that Traild is an E-Verify employer.

A Brief Overview
The Clinical Vector Core (CVC) is a division of the Raymond G. Perelman Center for Cellular and Molecular Therapeutics (CCMT) at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. The CCMT fosters a multidisciplinary approach to develop cures for debilitating and life-threatening genetic disorders using innovative gene and cell therapy approaches. CVC operations include manufacturing, quality control testing, and certification of recombinant adeno-associated and lentiviral viral vectors for use as Investigational Drugs in pre-clinical and early-phase clinical studies. CVC operations comply with FDA's current Good Manufacturing Practice regulations and other regulatory standards and guidelines applicable to early-phase Investigational Drugs. Vectors are made available to clinical programs in academia, industry and government in the U.S. and abroad. --- This role plays a vital role in the day-to-day operations of the Clinical Vector Core to assure the highest achievable quality and consistency of products, adherence to standards established in the CVC, and compliance with cGMP regulations. Manufacturing involves aseptic processing in a pharmaceutical cleanroom facility, large-scale cell culture, viral vector generation, purification, concentration, and fill & finish operations, according to established standard operating procedures (SOPs) and specifications. This role will work independently and self-directed and is involved in personnel training and supervising junior personnel as required. The employee will also participate in and assist with planning and coordination, reviewing of records, drafting of documents, and training and supervision of junior personnel commensurate with experience. The position requires good documentation practices, aseptic processing, team work, and an ability to consistently perform delicate tasks according to established procedures in a manufacturing environment. The position requires the employee to consistently exercise discretion and judgment in execution of experiments and of data derived. All employees are responsible for compliance with written policies and procedures and for correctness, truthfulness, timeliness, legibility, integrity, and accuracy when recording data and observations in compliance with current cGMP regulations.

As an Advisor or Senior Policy Advisor, you will play a pivotal role in crafting robust policy advice for senior leaders and Ministers aligned with DOC's strategic direction and Treaty obligations.

We are recruiting for 3 x fixed term/secondment roles (until March 2028) across these teams- Hunting & Fishing, Regulatory Systems and Budget & Funding but you will be flexible to work across different policy areas as team priorities shift.

title: Computer Based Training Specialist
description:
Index Analytics, LLC, is a rapidly growing, Baltimore-based small business providing health-related consulting services to the federal government. At the center of our company culture is a commitment to instilling a dynamic and employee-friendly place to work. We place a priority on promoting a supportive and collegial team environment and enhancing staff experience through career development and educational opportunities.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We’re looking for a CBT Training Specialist to support the design, development, delivery, maintenance, and continuous improvement of computer-based training and eLearning materials for federal healthcare programs. This role will assess training needs; develop learner-centered content using tools such as Articulate 360/Storyline 360; and create practical training aids, curricula, scripts, assessments, scenarios, knowledge checks, and accessible learning materials that help users understand systems, processes, data, and operational workflows.

The CBT Training Specialist will work closely with program stakeholders, subject matter experts, product teams, and end users to identify training requirements, apply instructional design best practices, and build engaging training products that support adoption, knowledge transfer, and performance improvement. This position requires strong facilitation, instructional design, communication, analytical, accessibility, and quality review skills, with the ability to translate complex business and technical information into clear, engaging, Section 508-compliant training content and support LMS-based course delivery and tracking.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Collaborate with the team, assuming responsibility to create and adapt learning content for diverse audiences and various eLearning formats.
  • Develop modules using Articulate 360 products, mainly Storyline 360 including interactive simulations.
  • Incorporate accessibility into modules, including closed captions, alt text, and screen reader focus order.
  • Coordinate with subject-matter experts (SMEs) to gather information for modules.
  • Apply Instructional Design models utilizing ADDIE and Blooms Taxonomy to develop and implement module structures and content.
  • Use a combination of source materials and content-gathering meetings to write voiceover scripts, distilling technical, complex information into well-organized, easily digestible material.
  • Create effective, aesthetically pleasing presentation/slide designs, infographics, templates, etc. Incorporate branding guidelines.
  • Build creative, engaging learner-centered knowledge checks and activities.
  • Conduct peer reviews. Perform testing and provide valuable feedback regarding script and text, audio, design, functionality, and user friendliness.
  • Present eLearning modules at various stages of development to the team/SMEs/stakeholders to garner feedback, assess progress, or shift direction as needed.
  • Update and maintain modules as required.
  • Assist in the evaluation of training effectiveness and provide recommendations for improvements.
  • Work with Learning Management Systems (LMS) to upload, manage, and track courses, ensuring a seamless experience for learners.
  • Write team documentation, detailing eLearning processes, procedures, checklists, and guides.

description:
Loula is seeking experienced postpartum doulas to join our growing network of independent doula providers! You must complete this interest form to move forward in our process! We're excited to hear from you!

✨ About Loula

With a network of over 500 experienced and diverse doulas, Loula is building the leading provider network for birth and postpartum doula care. We partner with both Medicaid and commercial health insurance plans to make it easier for doulas to accept health insurance without the administrative burden.

Loula offers full-service support for Medicaid enrollment, credentialing, insurance verification, medical billing, and payment to doulas in California. By taking on the operational complexity, Loula empowers doulas to focus on what matters most: delivering exceptional care.

We believe every family deserves access to high-quality postpartum support, not just those who can afford to pay out of pocket. Our mission is to help doulas build thriving practices while making it possible for insured families to access the care they deserve.

💰 Why Partner with Loula?

We partner with our doulas every step of the way:

  • How much can I make? Up to $134/hour of billable time, with rates varying by payer and plan.

  • Direct deposits twice a month. Don't worry about denied claims! We pay you regardless of claim outcomes, so you're never left waiting on payers to get paid.

  • Free, hassle-free credentialing: We get you credentialed with major Medicaid and commercial insurance plans in California, at no cost to you.

  • Client referrals, not cold outreach: Get referrals to insured clients through our client referral/doula matching program. Let our Care Navigator introduce you to amazing clients, no marketing spend required on your end.

🛠 Minimum Qualifications

You'll need:

  • 5 years of experience as a doula, with 3 letters of recommendation OR

  • If you've trained as a birth/full-spectrum doula, 16 hours of birth/full-spectrum doula training and attendance at 3 births as a doulaa

You'll also need:

  • Adult and infant CPR training

  • HIPAA training

If you don't yet have CPR training, HIPAA training, liability insurance, or the letters of recommendation, you can still reach out! We can support you in getting set up with these requirements.

We're looking for an experienced and highly capable professional to join our Revenue Services and Projects team and play a key role in delivering some of NZTA's most significant business, revenue and technology initiatives.

title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) - Outbound/Flow, AFT Outbound Execution Teams
description:
Are you seeking an environment where you can apply state-of-the-art computer science techniques, work with latest tools and technologies, and use huge amounts of data to solve real-world problems and make a massive impact? Come and join us in the Outbound group within Amazon Fulfillment Technologies!

Amazon Fulfillment Technologies builds software, hardware, and processes that help tens of thousands of employees deliver billions of items a year from over eighty warehouses worldwide. We ensure that you get what you want when we promised it to you. We are at the core of Amazon's business and our software is mission-critical.

The Outbound Execution group, based in Toronto, creates the software that makes it easy for Amazon staff to safely, quickly and accurately perform the most labour-intensive warehouse function: picking the items for your order. We deal with real physical processes, and our systems need to make decisions within real-time constraints. At our scale, a small optimization can instantly help thousands of staff and save Amazon millions of dollars: savings we can pass on to our customers to keep our prices low. We also have the opportunity to work with the most advanced technologies: AWS, robotics, machine learning, and augmented reality among others.

As a software engineer at Amazon, you're responsible for much more than just writing robust, reliable, scalable and readable code. You will operate a platform where any downtime costs millions. You will work directly with the users of your software, to deeply understand the domain and identify opportunities for improvements and optimizations. We are looking for true engineers that find practical technology solutions to real problems.
Learn more about Amazon's warehouses & software engineering:









Key job responsibilities
You will own the design and operation of high-scale, event-driven backend services powering Amazon's shipment and delivery data platform. In this role you will:

* Own end-to-end delivery of distributed services (SNS/SQS, AWS Lambda) that process and publish shipment events consumed across Amazon — from design through multi-region rollout (NA, EU, FE) and production operations.
* Lead complex service and data migrations, consolidating downstream consumers onto shared platform services with minimal disruption to dependent teams.
* Make integration and data-sharing decisions for partner teams — evaluating new event subscriptions for scalability, security, and correct scope.
* Raise the operational excellence bar for your services: monitoring, alarming, on-call, and reducing systemic toil.
* Navigate ambiguity to scope and sequence work, influence technical direction, and unblock dependencies across teams.

About the team
The Shipment Data Platform (SDP) team sits at the heart of Amazon's outbound fulfillment flow. We are the interface between Amazon's fulfillment network and the systems that turn a customer's order into a shipment — processing fulfillment requests, coordinating shipment messages, and serving as the trusted platform for shipment data. Every day our services get millions of shipments moving. Our culture is hands-on, ownership-driven, and collaborative. We care deeply about operational excellence and favor pragmatic solutions over needless complexity. Engineers at every level own meaningful pieces of the platform. If you enjoy building resilient distributed systems with real impact, you'll feel at home here.

title: Billing Clerk (Limited Term)
description:
Salud Para La Gente (SALUD) provides high quality, comprehensive and cost-effective medical, dental, behavioral health, optometry and other services to underserved, low-income communities in the Monterey Bay area, including Santa Cruz and Monterey Counties. SALUD began in Watsonville in 1978 as a storefront free clinic, and became a FQHC (Federally Qualified Health Center) in 1992. With four health center sites, satellite and school-based health centers and over 400 employees, we provide high quality services to patients of all ages.


Under immediate supervision (Billing Clerk I), or general supervision (Billing Clerk II/III), of the Billing Supervisor or Manager, the Billing Clerk performs a full range of billing and revenue cycle support functions to ensure accurate, timely, and compliant processing of patient encounters and claims. This position supports organizational financial health by managing patient accounts, resolving billing issues, working with clinical and administrative staff, and providing responsive customer service to patients and payers.

This position supports the organization's mission, vision, and values through excellence and competence, collaboration, innovation, respect, commitment to our community, and accountability and ownership.


DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:

Billing Clerk I: This is the entry-level, trainee class in the Billing Clerk series. Incumbents perform routine billing support duties while learning applicable systems, payer requirements, departmental procedures, and revenue cycle operations. Work is performed under close supervision with detailed instructions and review.

Billing Clerk II: This journey-level classification performs a full range of standard billing, payment posting, claim follow-up, and account resolution duties under general supervision. Incumbents independently process routine work using established procedures and resolve common discrepancies.

Billing Clerk III: This journey-level classification performs, in addition to any Billing Clerk II responsibilities, the most complex or specialized billing functions requiring extensive knowledge of payer rules, billing systems, and revenue cycle processes. Incumbents resolve complex account issues, recurring claim problems, and non-routine discrepancies requiring the most independent judgment.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Consistently adhere to SPLG communication guidelines and maintain professional interactions with patients, peers, and supervisors.
  2. Support patients with billing matters through effective communication.
  3. Respond to patient inquiries regarding balances, bills, or account correspondence professionally and timely; answer incoming calls courteously using proper phone etiquette.
  4. Task the Patient Service Representatives to update registrations or correct registration mistakes; charge posting and assist in payment posting across Salud specialties and payers accurately and confidentially within the practice management system; provide billing support and billing-related technical assistance to staff, clinical and administrative, as needed.
  5. Process encounters and claims, including reviews for errors, coordinating corrections, preparing batches for submission, and logging issues for reporting.
  6. Manage aged receivables and claim denials, change or correct billing codes, organize insurance correspondence and ensure accurate payments. This includes supporting payment posting, credit balance review, refunds, reconciliation activities, and coordination with Finance on revenue tracking and audits.
  7. Receive billing or revenue cycle in-service training and meetings as needed.
  8. Provide office support and backup for billing department functions, including posting charges and payments and preparing claims, assisting with month-end close.
  9. Coordinate with clinical staff to correct registration, missing charges/forms, and billing code issues (diagnosis, CPT/CDT/HCPCS).
  10. Communicate clinic payment policies and financial arrangements to patients.
  11. Maintain effective working relationships with diverse patients, employees, and partners.
  12. Support administrative tasks such as faxing, scanning, or sending patient financial records.
  13. Manage delinquent accounts by establishing and monitoring payment arrangements.
  14. Adhere to SPLG Mission, Vision, Values, Standards of Conduct, and HIPAA principles.
  15. Perform other billing duties as assigned.

title: Nlyte DCIM Consultant
description:
CONSULTANT JOB DESCRIPTION
Nlyte DCIM Consultant | NEO Specialist

Arganteal Corp. | Full-Time Contract, 6 Months | Hybrid: 50% Onsite / 50% Remote


Engagement Terms

  • Contract Type: Full-time contract, 1099 to your SS# or EIN
  • Duration: 6 months
  • Work Structure: Hybrid — 50% onsite / 50% remote
  • Onsite Locations: Dallas Fort Worth area data centers (both DFW locations), with additional site work in Austin and Houston
  • Travel & Expenses: Reimbursed for onsite work
  • Rate: Negotiated based on scope and experience
  • Availability: Candidates should be available for project ramp within 1 to 2 weeks of agreement

About the Engagement

We are seeking an experienced Nlyte DCIM Consultant with demonstrated, hands-on expertise in Nlyte Energy Optimizer (NEO) to support client deployments, optimization engagements, and subject matter advisory work.
This is a full-time contract engagement running 6 months, structured as hybrid work: 50% onsite and 50% remote. Onsite work will take place at data centers in the Dallas Fort Worth area (both DFW locations), with additional site work in Austin and Houston. Travel and expenses for onsite work are reimbursed.

Role Summary

The Nlyte DCIM Consultant — NEO Specialist serves as the primary technical authority on Nlyte Energy Optimizer for Arganteal's clients. You will deploy, configure, optimize, and advise on NEO within enterprise and government data center environments, working across facilities, IT operations, and sustainability stakeholder groups to deliver measurable improvements in energy visibility, capacity planning, and operational efficiency.

Core Responsibilities

  • Deploy and configure Nlyte Energy Optimizer (NEO) in greenfield and brownfield data center environments, including protocol-based device polling, power chain modeling, and dashboard buildout.
  • Document and map the full electrical power chain from utility feeds, generators, and batteries through switchgear, PDUs, and branch circuits to end devices.
  • Establish real-time energy monitoring across power distribution and cooling infrastructure, including branch circuit monitoring and threshold alerting.
  • Build and validate power failure simulations and redundancy models to identify single points of failure and support risk reduction planning.
  • Deliver capacity planning analysis linking energy and power data to space, cooling, and infrastructure growth projections.
  • Produce and tune standard and custom NEO reports for operational, finance, and sustainability audiences covering PUE, power usage, circuit utilization, device performance, and efficiency metrics.
  • Integrate NEO with NAO (Nlyte Asset Optimizer), CMDB, ITSM, BMS, and virtualization platforms as required by engagement scope.
  • Identify underutilized or misaligned power and cooling resources and deliver actionable optimization recommendations.
  • Support colocation and multi-tenant environments including tenant-level energy visibility and SLA-aligned reporting.
  • Provide advisory services to data center operations, facilities, IT leadership, finance, and sustainability stakeholders.
  • Produce engagement documentation including runbooks, configuration records, data integrity standards, and as-built deliverables.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of hands-on Nlyte Energy Optimizer (NEO) implementation and configuration experience in production data center environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain NEO power chain models from utility to end device, including AC and DC power documentation.
  • Proficiency with NEO protocol-based polling (Modbus, SNMP, BACnet, and others) and hardware-agnostic device integration.
  • Experience delivering NEO capacity planning, branch circuit monitoring, and power failure simulation deliverables.
  • Working knowledge of data center power and cooling fundamentals: PUE, power density, redundancy tiers, CRAC/CRAH systems, and UPS configurations.
  • Familiarity with Nlyte NAO (Asset Optimizer) and the relationship between energy data and asset lifecycle management.
  • Strong documentation and reporting skills; able to produce client-ready deliverables for both technical and executive audiences.
  • Experience working in enterprise, federal, or colocation data center environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Former Nlyte Software or Carrier professional services experience.
  • Experience with NEO integrations to ServiceNow, BMC Remedy, or other ITSM/CMDB platforms.
  • Familiarity with Nlyte BMS integrations (WebCtrl / Automated Logic, Johnson Controls, Siemens).
  • Experience supporting DCOI (Data Center Optimization Initiative) compliance reporting for federal clients.
  • Knowledge of ESG and sustainability reporting frameworks as applied to data center energy consumption.
  • ITIL Foundation or equivalent service management certification.
  • BICSI, CDCP, CDCS, or similar data center infrastructure credentials.
  • Familiarity with Nlyte Intelligence, Placement and Optimization, or Nlyte Insight modules.

What Good Looks Like

The right candidate has built Nlyte from the ground up in complex environments, not just administered it. You understand how an improperly modeled power chain undermines the entire DCIM environment. You have taken a client from spreadsheets and tribal knowledge to a live, accurate NEO deployment. You can walk a facilities team through branch circuit monitoring setup and walk a CFO through an energy cost reduction report in the same week. You know the difference between what NEO is capable of and what most clients have actually turned on.

We believe every birthing person deserves access to high-quality doula support, not just those who can afford to pay out of pocket. Our mission is to help doulas build thriving practices while making it possible for insured families to access the care they deserve.

💰 Why Partner with Loula?

We partner with our doulas every step of the way:

  • How much can I make? Up to $134/hour of billable time, with rates varying by payer and plan.

  • Direct deposits twice a month. Don't worry about denied claims! We pay you regardless of claim outcomes, so you're never left waiting on payers to get paid.

  • Free, hassle-free credentialing: We get you credentialed with major Medicaid and commercial insurance plans in California, at no cost to you.

  • Client referrals, not cold outreach: Get referrals to insured clients through our client referral/doula matching program. Let our Care Navigator introduce you to amazing clients, no marketing spend required on your end.

  • Build your own practice, your way: You're an independent contractor in a non-exclusive network, so keep your own clients and practice alongside your work with Loula.

  • No minimums, no pressure: There are no client minimums or visit requirements. You decide how much or how little to take on.

  • Admin? Handled: We manage insurance verification, billing, and payment so you can spend your time with clients, not paperwork.

  • You're not alone: Join a network of experienced doulas with access to shared resources, community, and ongoing support.

🛠 Minimum Qualifications

You'll need one of the following:

  • Completed 16 hours of birth doula training AND attended 3 births as a doula, OR

  • 5 years of experience as a doula, with 3 letters of recommendation

You'll also need:

  • Adult and infant CPR training

  • HIPAA training

  • Liability insurance

If you don't yet have CPR training, HIPAA training, liability insurance, or the letters of recommendation, you can still reach out! We can support you in getting set up with these requirements.

Please note that if you are not located in California and/or do not meet the minimum qualifications listed above, we will be unable to move forward with an introductory meeting.

📝 Application Process

How can I learn more about partnering with Loula?

  1. Click this link to submit an interest form and start the process

  2. You'll be prompted to complete a few basic screening questions

  3. If you meet the minimum qualifications, you'll be invited to schedule a call with our team

  4. During this conversation, we'll get to know you, your experience, and your practice goals, and share more about how Loula works. This is meant to assess whether a partnership is a strong mutual fit.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.

title: Consultor Vendas | Marília, Presidente Prudente ou Lins (SP)
description:
A Zoetis valoriza e apoia a inclusão, prezando pela igualdade de oportunidades.

Localidade: Marília, Presidente Prudente ou Lins (SP)

SUMÁRIO DA POSIÇÃO

Responsável pelo planejamento, realização e acompanhamento das vendas aos canais de varejo e distribuição do seu setor de acordo com a política comercial, assim como pela identificação de oportunidades e implantações de ações de estímulo a vendas, visando explorar ao máximo o potencial do território e atingir os objetivos comerciais, financeiros e de marketing propostos.

RESPONSABILIDADES DO CARGO

  • Assegurar que os objetivos comerciais e financeiros da Zoetis sejam alcançados em seu território, incluindo objetivos de venda, mix, preço, penetração e de valorização de marca;
  • Implantar e gerenciar a Política Comercial em seu setor de vendas, assegurando a correta classificação e segmentação dos canais;
  • Liderar a construção e a execução do Plano Estratégico Conjunto com os canais, com objetivo de positivação das marcas e atingimento das metas de sell-out e de sell-in;
  • Elaborar o Planejamento de Vendas do setor com base nas cotas recebidas, juntamente com a equipe do setor;
  • Mapear, estabelecer, cultivar e gerenciar relacionamento com tomadores de decisão e influenciadores de cada canal de comercialização (Distribuidores, Atacadistas, Revendas e Cooperativas);
  • Monitorar constantemente o nível de estoque dos seus canais, tomando as ações necessárias.
  • Identificar oportunidades e promover ações, em parceria com os canais, buscando estimular o giro dos produtos;
  • Implementar as ações de Trade Marketing definidas pela BU nos canais da sua responsabilidade, monitorando os resultados;
  • Implementar e acompanhar ações de merchandising nos canais diretos, visando uma melhor apresentação, comunicação da mensagem do produto e maximização do retorno dos investimentos realizados;
  • Assegurar a capacitação e engajamento da força de vendas dos canais atendidos sobre produtos e campanhas Zoetis através de reuniões, treinamentos e vistas acompanhadas;
  • Realizar treinamentos técnico-comerciais da linha Zoetis para equipe de vendas dos canais, visando a oferta adequada dos produtos aos consumidores finais;
  • Registrar as interações com os canais na ferramenta CRM e atingir os objetivos estabelecidos.
  • Prospectar constantemente novos canais, com objetivo de ampliar/renovar carteira de cliente e explorar o potencial do território;
  • Implantar as estratégias de acesso ao mercado em seu setor, buscando ampliar a disponibilidade, penetração da linha de produtos da Zoetis, assim como o desenvolvimento de novos mercados;
  • Conhecer e monitorar constantemente o desempenho dos produtos/linhas Zoetis dentro dos canais e em relação aos concorrentes;
  • Monitorar e reportar as ações da concorrência nos canais disponíveis;
  • Acompanhar os pedidos, desde que são realizados até o seu pagamento, interagindo – quando necessário com as áreas internas;
  • Zelar pelo bom estado dos equipamentos da área sob sua responsabilidade;
  • Zelar pela confidencialidade das informações sob sua responsabilidade;
  • Cumprir as normas e regulamentos contidos no Código de Conduta da empresa.

RELAÇÕES ORGANIZACIONAIS

Gerente de Vendas, Coordenador de Demanda, Assistente Tecnico, Gerente de Produto, Efetividade de Vendas, Logistica, Serviços de Marketing, Administração de Vendas, Financeiro.

RECURSOS GERENCIADOS

  • Vendas aos canais do seu setor, orçamento de gastos.

SUPERVISÃO

Para esta posição não se reporta nenhum colaborador diretamente. No entanto, ele(a) lidera e influencia indiretamente um time multifuncional.

EDUCAÇÃO / EXPERIÊNCIA

Educação:

Preferencialmente gradução em Veterinária ou relacionado. --- Administração de empresas, Economia, Engenharia, Zootecnia, Agronomia

Idiomas:

Inglês intermediário; Espanhol (desejável).

Experiência:

  • Mínimo de 7 anos de experiência em Vendas incluindo negociação, gestão de contas, gestão de canais e trade marketing;
  • Comprovada experiência no relacionamento com clientes, colegas e parceiros;

REQUISITOS DE HABILIDADES TÉCNICAS

  • Forte conhecimento da área de veterinária;
  • Habilidade na comunicação oral, escrita e interpessoal (incluindo palestras, apresentações, etc) e na liderança de pessoas (representante dos distribuidores);
  • Capacidade para trabalhar de forma independente e eficiente, influenciando distribuidores, supervisores e representantes de venda;
  • Habilidade para se relacionar com distribuidores, clientes e demais membros da equipe, promovendo as relações duradouras no espírito ganha-ganha;
  • Organização, planejamento e comprovada gestão eficiente do tempo, doterritório e de canais de acesso;
  • Domínio dos seguintes programas de informática: Excel, Word, PowerPoint e os sistemas de propriedade Zoetis, ou habilidade para aprender com rapidez;
  • Habilidade para aprender rapidamente informações técnicas e científicas, bem como de vendas;
  • Pró-atividade na realização de suas atividades;
  • Perfil alinhado aos objetivos, missão e visão da empresa, e com foco nos clientes.

  • High personal awareness, and growth mindset (for Software Engineer)

  • Experience with React, NodeJs, Typescript, Kafka, AWS or equivalent

Our team

title: Dish washer
description:
The Dishwasher is an essential member of MIKA's Back of House team. This position is responsible for maintaining a clean, organized, and sanitary kitchen by efficiently washing dishes, cookware, utensils, glassware, and kitchen equipment. The Dishwasher supports the entire culinary team by ensuring clean equipment and serviceware are consistently available throughout service.

The ideal candidate is reliable, hardworking, organized, team-oriented, and able to work efficiently in a fast-paced restaurant environment while maintaining high standards of cleanliness and sanitation.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Wash and sanitize dishes, plates, silverware, glassware, pots, pans, and kitchen equipment.
  • Operate the commercial dishwasher and follow proper washing and sanitizing procedures.
  • Maintain a clean and organized dish area throughout the shift.
  • Properly sort, rack, wash, dry, and store dishes and equipment.
  • Assist the kitchen team with maintaining adequate supplies of clean plates, utensils, cookware, and other equipment.
  • Keep floors, walls, sinks, drains, trash areas, and dishwashing areas clean and sanitary.
  • Empty trash and recycling and maintain proper waste disposal procedures.
  • Clean and sanitize work areas and equipment according to MIKA standards.
  • Assist with receiving, organizing, and storing deliveries when needed.
  • Support kitchen staff with basic cleaning and preparation tasks as directed.
  • Follow all food safety, sanitation, chemical handling, and workplace safety procedures.
  • Report broken or damaged equipment, dishes, glassware, or unsafe conditions to management.
  • Assist other Back of House team members whenever necessary.
  • Complete opening, closing, and side-work duties as assigned.
  • Maintain a professional, respectful, and positive attitude toward guests and team members.

Qualifications

  • Previous restaurant or dishwasher experience preferred but not required.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
  • Strong work ethic and reliability.
  • Ability to follow directions and work as part of a team.
  • Ability to maintain cleanliness and organization throughout the shift.
  • Basic understanding of food safety and sanitation is preferred.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, holidays, and varying schedules as required.
  • Must be able to stand for extended periods and perform physically demanding work.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Ability to lift and carry approximately 50 pounds.
  • Ability to bend, reach, push, pull, and lift throughout the shift.
  • Ability to work in a hot, wet, and fast-paced kitchen environment.
  • Ability to safely handle cleaning chemicals and equipment.

Performance Expectations

Success in this position is demonstrated through:

  • Consistent cleanliness and sanitation.
  • Timely availability of clean dishes and equipment.
  • Reliable attendance and punctuality.
  • Proper handling of equipment and chemicals.
  • Teamwork and communication.
  • Ability to maintain a clean and organized work area during busy service.
  • Compliance with MIKA policies and food safety standards.

ESPAÑOL

Resumen del Puesto

El Lavaplatos es un miembro esencial del equipo de Cocina de MIKA. Esta posición es responsable de mantener la cocina limpia, organizada y sanitaria, lavando eficientemente platos, utensilios, cristalería, ollas, sartenes y equipos de cocina.

El Lavaplatos apoya a todo el equipo culinario asegurándose de que los platos, utensilios y equipos limpios estén disponibles durante todo el servicio.

El candidato ideal debe ser responsable, trabajador, organizado, dispuesto a trabajar en equipo y capaz de trabajar eficientemente en un ambiente de restaurante de ritmo rápido, manteniendo altos estándares de limpieza y sanitización.

Responsabilidades Principales

  • Lavar y desinfectar platos, vajilla, cubiertos, cristalería, ollas, sartenes y equipos de cocina.
  • Operar correctamente el lavavajillas comercial y seguir los procedimientos de lavado y sanitización.
  • Mantener el área de lavado limpia y organizada durante todo el turno.
  • Clasificar, colocar, lavar, secar y almacenar correctamente los platos y equipos.
  • Apoyar al equipo de cocina asegurando la disponibilidad de platos, utensilios, ollas, sartenes y otros equipos limpios.
  • Mantener limpios y sanitizados los pisos, paredes, fregaderos, drenajes, áreas de basura y área de lavado.
  • Vaciar la basura y el reciclaje siguiendo los procedimientos establecidos.
  • Limpiar y desinfectar las áreas de trabajo y equipos de acuerdo con los estándares de MIKA.
  • Ayudar a recibir, organizar y almacenar entregas cuando sea necesario.
  • Apoyar al equipo de cocina con tareas básicas de limpieza y preparación según las instrucciones.
  • Cumplir con todos los procedimientos de seguridad alimentaria, sanitización, manejo de productos químicos y seguridad laboral.

  • Ayudar a otros miembros del equipo de Cocina cuando sea necesario.

description:
Job Summary

Resident Director is a live-in member of the University Housing team and is responsible for all aspects of the housing and residence life program in their assigned area. FGCU is building a culture of curiosity, commitment and collaboration. We value employees who successfully work with others and drive positive change through critical thinking and decisive action. Job Description

  • Serves on an on-call rotation to ensure the safety and welfare of residential students.
  • Provides good stewardship and fiscal management to all budgets for assigned areas or committees.

  • Other job-related duties as assigned.
