Davis Defense Group, Inc. has secured a stellar reputation as one of the premier Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) in the aerospace and defense industry, steadfastly supporting the Department of Defense since 2002. A critical combination of vision and dedication to excellence has helped our customers achieve numerous significant milestones on schedule and within budget. Today we employ over 700 personnel around the globe in a mix of analytical, advisory, technical, and support positions. The common thread across our organization is our commitment to our customers and an unwavering dedication to our principle motto: “Mission Focused, Future Ready. Innovating today, Leading tomorrow.”


Functional Description:


Davis Defense Group, Inc. (DDG) is seeking an Expeditionary Warfare School Distance Education Program (EWSDEP) curriculum Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support the U.S. Marine Corps College of Distance Education and Training (CDET) in Quantico Virginia. This position will support development of onsite and online distance education curriculum for company grade officer Professional Military Education (PME).


Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Adapt resident EWS curriculum into distance education curriculum using the Marine Corps Instructional Systems Design/Systems Approach to Training and Education (MCISD/SATE) curriculum development process, and in accordance with Student Learning Outcomes approved by CG, EDCOM.
  • Revise and update courseware, including all assessments and faculty development materials according to CDET’s course development schedules.
  • Maintain and manage the master Learning Management System (LMS) course sites.
  • Create and safeguard course assessments, answer keys, and reference keys electronically.
  • Develop and maintain electronic exam-mapping products demonstrating appropriate linkages between issues for discussion and specific educational objectives and learning outcomes; and assessments and specific educational objectives and learning outcomes.
  • Maintain electronic files and version control of all courseware, curriculum and assessments to include documents, graphics, readings, electronic media and supporting information for the courses.
  • Answer questions from the field on all aspects of the course.
  • Support Faculty Development (FD) by developing recommendations for faculty standards unique to the respective course, and developing, updating and managing course LMS FD sites and course faculty guides.
  • Conduct Institutional Effectiveness/Institutional Research (IE/IR) analysis by analyzing student performance data; conducting test item analyses for course assessment evaluation; analyzing end-of-course comments from students, faculty, commanders and outside stakeholders; preparing and analyzing descriptive statistics and graphical displays of End of Course (EOC) survey data; preparing electronic Course Content Review Board (CCRB) reports; and recommending curriculum changes to the Dean of Academics.
  • Participate in annual MCU faculty development sessions.
  • Teach a minimum of two EWSDEP courses each Academic Year (AY).
  • Attend the annual CDET Faculty workshop (normally 5 consecutive days) at Quantico VA in the summer months.

Required Experience:

  • Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF) experience (active duty or reserve).
  • Experience with and knowledge of all seven Warfighting Functions, with emphasis on Intelligence, Information, Logistics and Force protection.
  • Professional Military Education. Career Level School (CLS) graduate (resident or distance education).
  • Faculty experience, preferably using the Socratic method and with military PME programs/courses.
  • Curriculum development experience.

Desired Experience:

  • Experience in Amphibious operations, Crisis Response and Limited Contingency operations, and Counterinsurgency operations.
  • Current knowledge of USMC Force Design 2030 and Naval Integration initiatives.
  • Experience utilizing wargaming to achieve educational outcomes.
  • Experience with evaluating Generative Artificial Intelligence tools and integrating them into courseware and development processes.
  • Professional Military Education. Intermediate Level School (ILS) and/or Top Level School (TLS) graduate.
  • Experience with Learning Management Systems (LMS, e.g., Moodle).

Education Requirements:

  • Required: Bachelors Degree
  • Desired: Masters Degree in Military/Strategic Studies or related field

title: Industrial Painter
description:
McGee Corporation is seeking a dependable and detail-oriented Industrial Painter to join our manufacturing team. This position is responsible for preparing, painting, and maintaining structural steel products, including beams, columns, and fabricated components, while ensuring quality finishes and maintaining a safe, clean, and efficient work environment.


The ideal candidate will have at least one (1) year of industrial or construction painting experience, a strong work ethic, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.


Schedule: Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM – 4:30 PM
Weekend overtime may be required based on production needs.


Responsibilities

  • Paint structural steel products, including beams, columns, and fabricated components, according to company quality standards.
  • Ensure all products moving through the steel line receive the required coating in the designated paint booth.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and safe work areas at all times.
  • Clean and maintain paint guns, spray tips, respirators, paint booths, and other painting equipment to ensure proper operation.
  • Monitor paint inventory and notify the supervisor when supplies need to be reordered.
  • Replace paint gun spray tips after every 75–80 gallons of paint sprayed.
  • Clean and maintain the steel line paint booth, back paint booth, shot blaster, wood-cutting area, steel loading area, and surrounding work areas daily.
  • Clean and change filters on all paint pumps each day.
  • Replace protective wall coverings, floor coverings, and paint booth filters as needed to maintain quality and cleanliness.
  • Keep conveyor rollers, paddle conveyors, and conveyor chains free of paint buildup and debris.
  • Assist with cleaning the shot blaster when needed.
  • Assist with cutting boards, loading steel, and securing materials on trailers or in designated loading areas as required.
  • Follow all company safety procedures, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support manufacturing operations.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of one (1) year of industrial or construction painting experience required.
  • Experience operating industrial paint spraying equipment preferred.
  • Completion of a formal apprenticeship, vocational training, or equivalent on-the-job training is a plus.
  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing quality work.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
  • Reliable attendance and a strong work ethic.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand for extended periods while painting and performing production duties.
  • Ability to climb, bend, stoop, squat, kneel, and maintain balance throughout the workday.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 75 pounds.
  • Ability to safely work around industrial painting equipment, conveyors, and manufacturing machinery.
  • Ability to wear required personal protective equipment, including respirators and other safety equipment.

Benefits

McGee Corporation offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Health Savings Account (HSA)
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Company Matching Contributions
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Paid Holidays
  • Company-paid Life Insurance
  • Disability Insurance

At McGee Corporation, we're committed to quality, safety, and continuous improvement. Our employees are the foundation of our success, and we foster a workplace built on teamwork, respect, and craftsmanship. If you're looking for an opportunity to build your career with a company that values excellence and offers outstanding benefits and a positive work culture, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Intern, Rail Operations
description:
Job Description

College Intern – Regional Rail

Under direct supervision, supports OCTA’s Rail initiatives by assisting with compiling and analyzing rail performance data, preparing presentations and reports, attending and summarizing Committee and Board meetings, graphic design, and supporting special projects. The position will also provide opportunities to participate in field work and gain firsthand exposure to rail and transit operations, programs, and projects.

You will perform a variety of professional entry-level duties related to your major field of study and the sponsoring department's current business operations. As a College Intern, you will be exposed to OCTA's career opportunities in the transportation industry. You will gain deeper awareness of transportation's many facets through your OCTA orientation, projects and teams, and internal networking.

OCTA's College Intern Program is a year-round paid student/intern program. You will gain real world work experience on meaningful projects under the guidance of a transportation professional. You will have the opportunity to use problem solving, communication and decision-making skills as you gain valuable work experience. You will also work with a mentor and benefit from career counseling.

The pay range is from $20.00 - $23.00 per hour depending on your education level. This position is not eligible for employee benefits. The work schedule will consist of approximately 20 hours a week, not to exceed 1,000 hours within a continuous 12-month period.

This posting will remain open until a candidate is selected.

What You’ll Do

  • Prepare presentations, reports, and materials highlighting rail performance metrics, including ridership and on-time performance.
  • Support analysis of rail system performance data and trends.
  • Assist with rail program, budget, and project tracking.
  • Attend Committee and Board of Directors meetings and prepare meeting notes and summaries.
  • Participate in rail and transit field work to gain firsthand industry experience.
  • Conduct research and complete special projects related to rail and transit.
  • Compile and organize data for reports, presentations, and decision-making.
  • Support document control, file organization, and records management activities.

What We’re Looking For

  • Currently enrolled full-time college student (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, or Senior) at an accredited two- or four-year college or university
  • Pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree relevant to transportation, planning, business administration, engineering, data analytics, public administration or a related discipline
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills
  • Interest in public transportation, rail operations, transportation planning or related areas
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines
  • Ability to learn technical concepts and take on increasingly responsible assignments.
  • Detail-oriented, dependable, and comfortable working collaboratively in a professional environment.

Why You’ll Love It Here

  • Gain real-world transportation experience while working on rail and transit programs that serve Orange County.
  • Turn data into insights by working with ridership, on-time performance, and other key rail metrics.
  • See transportation in action through opportunities to participate in rail and transit field work.
  • Learn how public agencies operate through exposure to projects, budgets, programs, and OCTA’s Committee and Board processes.
  • Build your professional network while learning alongside experienced transportation professionals.
  • Strengthen your resume with meaningful projects and practical experience related to your field of study.

Join a team where innovation, integrity, and strategic thinking are valued.
Apply now to gain meaningful experience and contribute to OCTA’s transportation initiatives.

title: Associate Therapist Training Program
description:
At Evolve Treatment Centers, you’ll have the opportunity to bring your clinical skills to a team that genuinely cares—working in a supportive, collaborative environment where growth (yours and your clients’) is the priority.

Our Associate Therapist Training Program is designed for early-career clinicians who want hands-on experience working with adolescents navigating acute mental health challenges. You’ll gain exposure to both residential and outpatient settings while building confidence in your clinical voice and skillset.

In this role, you’ll support residential programs programs by completing biopsychosocial assessments, stepping into the role of Primary Therapist for assigned clients, and providing coverage as needed. As a Primary Therapist, you’ll lead DBT skills groups, facilitate individual and family therapy, and complete clinical documentation within required timelines.

We’re looking for someone who’s curious, motivated, and ready to learn—someone who can thrive in a fast-paced environment while staying grounded and client-centered. You’ll receive consistent clinical supervision, along with ongoing training and shadowing opportunities to support your growth.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide individual and family therapy for teens and their families
  • Complete biopsychosocial assessments (with support and independently over time)
  • Collaborate with the clinical team during weekly treatment meetings
  • Participate in weekly training track supervision to deepen your understanding of acute care
  • Partner with Residential Counselors to reinforce effective behavioral interventions
  • Co-facilitate—and eventually lead—DBT skills groups
  • Complete treatment plans, weekly reviews, and all required clinical documentation

Requirements:

  • Master’s degree in Clinical Psychology, Counseling, or Social Work
  • Active California BBS associate number (AMFT, ACSW, or APCC)
  • California DL and willingness to travel between Tarzana, Woodland Hills, Agoura Hills, and Calabasas locations

Schedule and Compensation

  • Schedule: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:30 PM (full-time, onsite)
  • Pay: $33–34/hour


Are you ready to make a meaningful impact in the lives of adolescents? At Evolve Treatment Centers, we offer a unique opportunity to combine clinical expertise with compassionate care in a supportive, team-based environment.

The Associate Therapist training program provides a unique opportunity for clinicians to gain experience working with teens facing acute mental health issues, as well as understanding residential and intensive outpatient settings. The Associate Therapist will provide clinical support to the residential and outpatient programs by completing Biopsychosocial Assessments, acting as a Primary Therapist to clients as assigned, and providing Primary Therapist coverage as assigned. Primary Therapist duties include, but are not limited to, running DBT Skills Training groups, providing individual and family therapy, and completing all clinical documentation within the required timelines. This individual should be eager to learn and comfortable with a fast-paced environment. Clinical supervision will be provided, as well as several other training and shadowing opportunities.

Job Duties:

  • Provide individual and family therapy to teens and their families
  • Conduct biopsychosocial assessments upon admission both with assistance from Primary Therapists and independently
  • Attend weekly clinical treatment teams and collaborate with clinicians to carry out individualized treatment plans
  • Attend weekly Training Track supervisions with peers to learn and understand acute care services
  • Participate in individual supervision when directly assigned cases
  • Provide case management support and coordinate with After-Care manager to ensure clients have appropriate discharge plans
  • Coach and collaborate with Residential Counselors to ensure effective behavioral interventions are carried-out with clients
  • Participate in, and eventually lead, DBT skills groups
  • Complete weekly treatment plan reviews, master treatment plans, other required clinical documentation

Requirements:

  • Master’s degree in clinical psychology, Counseling, or Social Work
  • Active BBS associate number (AMFT/ACSW/APCC)
  • 1-year minimum training commitment requested
  • Must be willing to go to all our locations in Tarzana, Woodland Hills, Agoura Hills, Calabasas.

Hours: Monday-Friday 9 am - 5:30 pm. This is a full-time, onsite position.
Payrate: $33-34/hour

description:

Leadership Support

Innovation is part of our DNA! Our goal is to be Earth's most customer-centric company, and we are just getting started. We need people who want to join an ambitious program that continues to push the state of the art in space-based systems design and wireless systems.

We're dedicated to supporting new team members. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. title: Hardware Test Engineer
description:
Gritt is an intelligent system that combines robotics and AI to build the infrastructure that pulls society forward. Gritt deploys via simple attachments to common equipment found on construction sites and autonomously performs labor-intensive tasks, verification, and planning. Gritt systems are already building critical infrastructure in the harshest outdoor environments, starting with large-scale solar. The founding team includes experts in robotics and AI from Carnegie Mellon, Stanford, and MIT. Gritt is backed by Obvious Ventures, Union Square Ventures, First Round Capital, Climactic, Congruent Ventures, and other leading firms.

Role: Hardware Test Engineer
Location: SF Bay Area (in-person)

About the role
We are looking for a Hardware Test Engineer to own how we prove our hardware is ready to survive years on a job site. Most of your testing happens in the yard behind our office, where our robots run in genuine sun, wind, dust, and temperature, alongside lab-based and life-cycle testing. You will define the test strategy, build the fixtures and automation that catch failures before they ship, and lead test campaigns across components, subassemblies, and fully integrated robots. Your work directly determines whether our hardware is trusted to hold up in the field.

What you'll get to work on

  • Own test strategy end to end - translate design requirements into test plans across components, subassemblies, and the fully integrated robot.

  • Run functional, environmental, and life-cycle testing (dust, heat, vibration, repeated cycling) to generate real numbers, not guesses.

  • Lead root-cause investigations on hardware failures - teardowns, data analysis, working directly with our hardware team to close the loop.

  • Test across real-world conditions the robot must handle in production, from new hardware to changing site and weather conditions.

  • Develop, document, and enforce safety procedures for testing heavy hardware around people and equipment.

  • Produce clear, data-driven test reports and maintain traceability from requirements through to test execution and results.

  • Investigate field incidents and feed structured findings back into the loop so the same issue never ships twice.


What we look for

  • B.S./M.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering, EE, Mechatronics, Robotics, or other engineering disciplines (or equivalent experience).

  • Monitor clinical safety data, including literature, case reports, and signal detection activities

  • Experience in clinical trial methodology, regulatory requirements, scientific methodology, and statistical principles, including authorship of scientific publications

  • Strong ability to analyse, interpret, and clearly communicate clinical safety data to diverse stakeholders

Desirable Skills

Our people are at the heart of everything we do. They bring their talent, passion and dedication to work with them every day. Their hard work inspires us and gives us purpose. We love working here together.

Here’s your chance to be a part of this story. If you’re ready to work in a place where your participation matters and your growth is a priority, we’re ready for you.

title: Compliance Supervisor
location: Port Kembla, New South Wales, Australia
description:
About Toll Group

At Toll, we do more than just logistics - we move the businesses that move the world. Our 16,000 team members can help solve any logistics, transport, or supply chain challenge – big or small. We have been supporting our customers for more than 130 years. Today, we support more than 20,000 customers worldwide with 500 sites in 27 markets, and a forwarding network spanning 150 countries. We are proudly part of Japan Post —

Global Logistics provides sophisticated supply chain solutions, from end-to-end or part solutions, warehousing and distribution to dedicated transport solutions, across the globe and to some of the most remote corners of the world.

We provide specialised integrated logistics services to customers in a range of industries including mining, chemical, gases, steel and plastics, petroleum, energy and Australian oil and gas industries and agriculture. Our customers operate in some of the most remote places on earth, 24 hours a day, seven days a week and require a logistics partner who can match their needs. We offer integrated value-based logistics solutions that bring greater operating efficiency and savings to our customers’ supply chains.

Compliance Supervisor – Port Kembla, NSW

Part Time 3 Days per week – flexible days or School Hours across 5 days per week

About the role and opportunity on offer –

We are seeking a Compliance Supervisor to join our transport operations team and play a critical role in maintaining a safe, compliant, and efficient transport network.

You will be responsible for overseeing compliance across drivers, subcontractors, fleet assets, and operational processes. This role will ensure adherence to Heavy Vehicle National Law (HVNL), Chain of Responsibility (CoR), NHVAS accreditation requirements, fatigue management obligations, vehicle maintenance standards, and customer-specific compliance requirements. This is an excellent opportunity for a compliance professional who enjoys working closely with operational teams, investigating issues, identifying improvement opportunities, and driving a strong culture of safety and accountability.

Transport industry experience is highly regarded but not essential. We welcome applications from candidates with backgrounds in compliance, safety, quality assurance, auditing, governance, or other highly regulated environments who are looking to apply their skills in the transport and logistics industry.

Key Responsibilities but not limited to –

  • Ensure compliance with HVNL, Chain of Responsibility (CoR), NHVAS accreditation requirements, customer obligations, and company policies across transport operations.

  • Monitor and manage NHVAS fatigue, mass management, and maintenance programs, including quarterly NHVR compliance reporting and annual management system reviews.

  • Investigate fatigue, mass, and other compliance breaches, maintain TRAC records, and implement corrective and preventative actions.

  • Conduct Work Diary audits and monitor driver compliance with Basic Fatigue Management (BFM) and legislative requirements.

  • Oversee fleet maintenance compliance, ensuring vehicle records remain current, audit-ready, and aligned with NHVAS standards.

  • Manage driver, vehicle, and subcontractor compliance, including licences, medicals, permits, inductions, qualifications, insurances, and competency requirements.

  • Maintain training matrices, coordinate compliance-related training and renewals, and support leaders in developing a strong culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.

About You –

To succeed in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • A proactive mindset and genuine passion for safety, compliance, governance, and operational excellence.

  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with operational teams, contractors, customers, and leadership groups.

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records, manage documentation, and ensure audit readiness across multiple compliance requirements.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with the confidence to review data, identify trends, investigate issues, and drive continuous improvement initiatives.

Why Join Us?

  • Join a safety-focused and compliance-driven organisation.

  • Play a key role in maintaining industry-leading transport standards.

  • Work closely with operational leaders and make a genuine impact on business performance.

If you're passionate about compliance, safety, and continuous improvement and want to play a critical role in supporting a high-performing operation, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today.

What moves you?

At Toll, you can help play a vital role in delivering what matters. From food, fuel, medicine and rescue services, we keep businesses and communities thriving. Every day brings change. We see that as an opportunity. To be curious. To ask the right questions. And build meaningful connections. Because finding new ways to solve problems is what we do. With a bold vision to expand our global reach, our 16,000+ people bring a passion for progress. We collaborate in friendly, caring teams, supported by approachable leaders who give us the autonomy to quickly make decisions with impact. Learn and grow with industry-leading training, alongside talented experts. Feel empowered to take on diverse challenges and new responsibilities to move you, our customers, and our world further.

Are you excited about this role but are concerned you don’t meet all the requirements? If you have similar skills and are willing to learn then we encourage you to apply anyway. We know that some people hesitate to apply for jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Toll, we value a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re interested in this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly then please talk to us – you may be just the right candidate for this or other roles we have coming up.

At Toll everyone is welcome including those of all ages, ethnicities, genders and abilities.

To find out more about us visit www.careers.tollgroup.com

You must be entitled to work in Australia and be prepared to undertake pre-employment checks including a criminal history check and medical.

title: Registrar
description:
Position Summary:


The Registrar is responsible for all academic record keeping including compilations, maintenance and tracking for student academic records. This comprises internal and external uses, maintenance of all students’ files including new, current, graduate, dropped and canceled students. The Registrar is also accountable for tasks, communication, and procedures for all graduation verification and processing. This position is required to work in a fast-paced environment while independently managing multiple tasks and projects with competing priorities and deadlines. All duties must be conducted in accordance with the mission, vision and core values of HCI; serving and assisting in a positive and professional manner for students, faculty and staff in the areas of customer service, respect, communication, collaboration and excellence. The Registrar must be able to demonstrate a sensitivity to the needs of students, faculty and staff as well as demonstrate commitment to HCI’s comprehensive learning programs. The Registrar works directly with faculty and staff to troubleshoot and resolve attendance issues. The Registrar is also responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, confidentiality and maintenance of student records in compliance with all federal, state and accreditation regulations and should be able to respond to all inquiries expected in an audit or accreditation process.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Registering new students.
  • Application maintenance and file coding.
  • Degree audit review.
  • Diploma ordering and processing.
  • Major/minor/concentration changes and other processes associated with degree completion/clearance.
  • Administrative matriculation of all new students.
  • Maintains and updates academic records and files for new, current and former students. Assures the integrity of files, folders, transcripts, grades, grade reports, and enrollment documentation for all students, entering grades and all pertinent student information into NEXUS.
  • Posts evaluated, nontraditional and transfer credit to students' records, including special titles and messages to permanent records and processes grade changes and tuition rebate requests.
  • Assesses and revises academic status for accuracy, performs clerical and receptionist duties involving proper handling of phone calls.
  • Researches, analyzes, and resolves student disputes as they relate to transfer credit, evaluations and graduation applications.
  • Enters and tracks all student attendance, reviewing accuracy immediately following class completion and aggressively tracks late grades.
  • Assists in processing student leaves of absence and withdrawals.
  • Verifies and records transcripts received for prospective students.
  • Determines when an applicant file is ready for evaluation. Enters applicant records into the learner database after the enrollment is approved by the Systems’ Registrar.
  • Manages all course registrations for current students and records all extensions.
  • Responsible for the accurate and punctual posting of final grades for courses at the end of each term.
  • Works cooperatively with other administrative departments and cohorts.
  • Regular and reliable attendance.
  • Comply with all governmental regulations and standards of accreditation.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

title: K-8 Spiritual Formation Advisor
description:
Valley Christian is seeking a K–8 Spiritual Formation Advisor to help oversee and cultivate a vibrant, Christ-centered spiritual life program across the K–8 campus in collaboration with the Director of Spiritual Life and school leadership. This role engages students, staff, parents, and the broader community through chapels, ministry development, retreats, service initiatives, and partnerships with families and local organizations, equipping culture changers for Christ.


Job Summary:


The K-8 Spiritual Formation Advisor (SFA) is responsible for directly and indirectly giving oversight of the spiritual life program on the K-8 campus, under the advisement and direction of the Director of Spiritual Life. The SFA interacts with students, staff, parents, and our extended community, helping to create, maintain, and improve a decidedly Christian culture at VCS. This position works closely with the Director of Spiritual Life and other school leadership, working alongside and supporting many departments at VCS. Under the direction of the Director of Spiritual Life, the SFA provides a particular focus on K-8 chapels, Ministry Development, trips and retreats, our expanding ENGAGE and Christian service program and supporting students and staff in their spiritual formation at the K-8. As needed, the SFA will also support our partnership with parents through Parent University, and relationships with local churches and parachurch organizations.


Role and Responsibilities:

  • Provides strategic and day-to-day oversight for all chapels at the 5-8 and K-4, including working with chapel coordinators or Ministry Development teams on each campus, theme development, securing speakers, and creative content. Additionally, provides direct support for 5-8 chapels by participating regularly in the Ministry Development class
  • Oversight for all aspects of spiritual life trips and retreats at the K-8, including the 8th grade trip (August) and Spiritual Emphasis Week (February)
  • Oversight for the expansion of the ENGAGE & Christian Service program to the K-8, working collaboratively with members of the Spiritual Life department and administration to establish and expand this program
  • Works alongside ENGAGE Manager to oversee daily K-8 ENGAGE operations, including coordination with volunteers, chaperones, and partnerships, trip selection, strategic direction, chaperone training, leadership training, travel logistics, ENGAGE Handbook, financial processes, and more
  • Alongside the Spiritual Life Director, Head of School, and Campus Principal, acts as one of the school's lead speakers/preachers/teachers at spiritual life and special VCS community events. Examples include chapels, retreats, conferences, and special events like Night of Worship, Christmas productions, graduation ceremonies, Parent University events, etc. Likely to average 10-20 speaking opportunities per school year
  • Leads pastoral-like guidance and spiritual formation for students on an individual basis, through small group mentorship, and fostering Biblical leadership across grade levels.
  • Works to ensure a robust spiritual culture among staff, which may include devotions, surveys, Bible studies, mentorships, training (Foundations of the Faith), etc.
  • Collaborate with Campus Principal, Spiritual Life Director, Bible Teachers (K-8), and Curriculum department regarding Bible curriculum, spiritual development, and theological issues for K-8 classes (especially Bible classes)
  • Work alongside Spiritual Life Director and other VCS leadership to administer, review, and impact measurements around the spiritual growth of students (most notably through the administration of the Flourishing Faith Index and other resources)
  • Collaborate with other VCS leadership to provide resources and training opportunities for VCS parents, primarily through Parent University.
  • Acts as a secondary point of contact for any and all ways in which the school partners with local churches
  • Adhere to Valley Christian policies, procedures/processes, and codes
  • Performs other related assigned duties
